about: The Loop Atlas model: every gameplay loop Cosmic Shore offers, from one input to the months-long game, on three layers (now, plan, prop). Hand-written source of truth for the loops ABOVE the kit; the kits are read from Docs/FleetCodex/abilities.json and the board from Docs/ElementalLoop/STATUS.md by Tools/Build/loop_atlas.py. Rules for editing: Docs/LoopAtlas/README.md.

layers.name: Now
layers.is: What is in the game today, with how far each loop has been played and signed off. A loop the plan has and the game lacks shows as a ghost.

layers.name: Planned
layers.is: The stabilised version the team has decided on: Garrett's elemental loop, the arcade restructure, voyages V1 to V4. Where the plan says nothing, it is a hole.

layers.name: Proposed
layers.is: The plan plus proposed changes. Every hole is filled with an invention, marked as one, for the team to accept, change or throw out.

tiers.is: One input and the hull's answer. The feel of flying.
tiers.ask: Is it a pleasure with nothing to do?

tiers.is: One elemental ability, from trigger to payoff and back to ready.
tiers.ask: Is the payoff worth the trigger, and where does the pleasure land?

tiers.is: Verbs chained inside one kit. The loops a kit has baked in.
tiers.ask: Does one verb set up the next?

tiers.is: The kit pointed at the game's goals: what this vessel does for its team.
tiers.ask: Does what I am good at matter to the objective?

tiers.is: One objective, won or lost: an arcade or arena match, or a cell on a voyage.
tiers.ask: Can I read who is winning and why, in about 90 seconds?

tiers.is: A sitting in one place: a ladder run, an arena set, a voyage.
tiers.ask: Do I want one more, and does anything point me to another place?

tiers.is: What changes between sittings: unlocks, the fleet, the squad, the crew, the hoard.
tiers.ask: What do I have tomorrow that I did not have today?

tiers.is: What changes without you: the living sea, sagas, the meta, new vessels.

drivers.name: Sensation
drivers.is: The raw joy of the movement itself.

drivers.name: Mastery
drivers.is: Getting better: a cleaner line, a harder rung.

drivers.name: Creation
drivers.is: Making mass, growing, building something that stays.

drivers.name: Destruction
drivers.is: Breaking mass. The release of a big hit.

drivers.name: Rivalry
drivers.is: Beating another pilot: a place, a petal, a claim.

drivers.name: Fellowship
drivers.is: Playing with and for a team or a party.

drivers.name: Discovery
drivers.is: Something new: a toy, a hull, an uncharted place.

drivers.name: Collection
drivers.is: Having it: vessels, pilots, artifacts, relics.

drivers.name: Stakes
drivers.is: Something of yours can be lost.

drivers.name: Story
drivers.is: People, factions and sagas that remember you.

drivers.name: Objective
drivers.is: Goals laid out on the map by the game you are in.

drivers.name: Reward
drivers.is: Crystals, pay and unlocks handed over at the end.

handoffs.name: Tank full
handoffs.is: A resource the loop was banking is full, so you go and spend it one tier up.

handoffs.name: Objective met
handoffs.is: The loop's goal is reached and the tier above takes its next step.

handoffs.name: Loss
handoffs.is: The loop is lost and the tier above resets or sends you home.

handoffs.name: Reward to spend
handoffs.is: You hold something that is only useful in another loop.

handoffs.name: Something new
handoffs.is: A new hull, card, place or piece of news opens a loop you have not run.

handoffs.name: A friend
handoffs.is: An invite or a party moves you to where someone else is.

handoffs.name: Enough of this
handoffs.is: The loop has stopped paying and you look for another at the same tier.

nodes.name: The long game
nodes.is: Everything the product offers a person over months. Each pass is a stretch of sittings that ends because the world, the fleet or the meta changed.

phases.d: Something pulled you in: a friend, news from the sea, a new hull, habit.
Home offers the Toybox, the Arcade, the Arena and Voyages.
Rounds in one place, sometimes crossing to another.
Crystals, quest progress, artifacts, standing, replays.
Spend and arrange: a vessel, a squad, a pilot, an artifact.
The sea ticks, sagas open, the meta is rebalanced, a vessel is added.

now.note: The places and most arcs exist. Nothing in the build changes on a schedule, so the last phase is empty today.

plan.note: The meta is rebalanced on a schedule by the elemental loop's step 5, voyages add a living sea with sagas and relics, and new vessels enter at step 1 and unsettle more than their own balance.

prop.note: Give the last phase a name and a clock: the Tide (see The Tide).

holes.q: How many sittings make one pass, and how often a person comes back, is not measured. Analytics events are declared but no funnel reads them yet.
holes.fill: Target 3 to 5 sittings a week and one Tide every 6 weeks. Measure it from game_started and game_completed per account before tuning anything above the Round.

nodes.name: A sitting
nodes.is: One time you open the game. Home is the hub: every change of place passes through it.

phases.d: The hub screen, with the menu freestyle flying behind it.
Toybox, Arcade, Arena or Voyage.
The place's own loop.
Placing, the scoreboard, the payout.
Rematch, another place, or the Hangar and the Ark.

nodes.repsOf: sittings per pass of the long game

now.note: Home, Hangar and Profile are open; the Ark screen is the Elemental Converter; Port is locked and the Store has no screen.

plan.note: Four places: Toybox, Arcade, Arena, Voyages. Voyages are the culminating experience.

prop.note: Add the breath between rounds so that crossing to another place is offered, never left to the menu.

holes.q: Nothing in the game points a player from one place to another. A crossing happens only if the player opens Home and thinks of it.
holes.fill: The breath (new loop): after each result, one offered next step chosen from what the round just trained.

holes.q: Rounds per sitting and places per sitting are not measured.
holes.fill: Aim for 5 to 8 rounds and 1 or 2 places in a sitting; read it from the analytics events.

nodes.name: The breath
nodes.is: Proposed. The pause between rounds, treated as a loop of its own: the one place where the game hands you up, down or across.

phases.d: Placing, plus the one number your role moved (time, petals, volume made and removed).
Crystals, a rung, a petal on the vessel's flower.
Rematch, next rung, or a crossing: 'this trained you for Regatta'.

prop.note: Proposal P5. The scoreboard already knows the placing and the volume books; this adds the hand-off.

nodes.name: Toybox
nodes.is: Freestyle. Nothing is scored. You fly, find toys and try hulls. It is also the menu's background, so every sitting starts inside it.

now.note: Toys are chosen in the Toy Box only (2026-11-01). The Vessel Changer is where every new hull first becomes flyable.

plan.note: Stays the place with no stakes and no artifacts. The Arkway is a taste of a voyage.

prop.note: Each toy ends by offering its scored cousin: the Vessel Changer offers the hull's Time game, the Arkway offers a voyage.

holes.q: What a toy session is for, in loop terms, is not written: there is no stated reason to leave a toy or to come back to one.
holes.fill: A toy's exit is a crossing. Every toy names the scored loop it is the free version of, and offers it when the player has done the toy's verb a few times.

nodes.name: Free flight
nodes.is: Flying a hull for its own sake in an open cell. The kit with no objective around it.

phases.n: Pick a line through the mass
Use a verb because it feels good
See what it did to the cell

nodes.name: The changers
nodes.is: Vessel Changer, Domain Changer and Element Charger: swap what you are and feel the difference at once.

phases.n: Pick a hull, a domain or an element level

now.note: Every new vessel is done when it can be flown from the Vessel Changer.

prop.note: After a few minutes in a hull you do not own, offer its Time game at I1.

src: Docs/ToySystem/ARCHITECTURE.md (Vessel Changer, Domain Changer, Element Charger)

nodes.name: Spawn Matrix and Cell Selector
nodes.is: Choose what the cell holds and which cell you are in, then play in it.

phases.n: Pick what to spawn or which cell

nodes.name: Painting
nodes.is: Connect the dots: fly strokes through rings until the picture is drawn, then share it.

phases.n: Fly a stroke through its rings
The picture is done: share it

nodes.name: Wanderway
nodes.is: Wander without the Ark: a conveyor of small scenes, one after another, until you turn back.

nodes.name: Arkway run
nodes.is: Wander with the Ark: one Ark, a corridor of cells, no map and nothing at stake. The most voyage-like toy.

phases.n: The crossing: fauna on the hull

plan.note: Stays a toy. Voyages reuse its machinery and do not change it.

nodes.name: Arcade
nodes.is: One vessel, scored. Every card seats a hull and teaches one element with it. This is where a kit is learned.

phases.d: All, Time, Charge, Mass-Space, Party.
The card seats its hull.
I1 intro, I2 fun, I3 challenging, I4 very hard.
Aimed at about 90 seconds for an experienced pilot.
Placing and the payout.

phases.n: Rematch, next rung or next card

now.note: The four categories and the filter landed 2026-11-17. About 80 hull-locked cards exist; most were built headless and never flown. One step is signed off by a person: Dolphin Time, fun.

plan.note: Every vessel has at least a Time game, a Charge game and a Mass-Space game. Time trains for Regatta, Charge for Broadside, Mass-Space for Brood Rush. Party games train for nothing.

prop.note: The result screen says what the round trained, and lights a petal on the vessel's flower.

holes.q: Rounds per run are not measured, and nothing but the player's own wish moves them from a card to the next card.
holes.fill: 3 to 5 rounds a run. The breath offers the next rung after a win and the same rung after a loss.

holes.q: Most cards have never been played: steps 1 to 3 of the elemental loop are 'built', not 'done', for every vessel and element except Dolphin Time step 1.

nodes.name: The rung ladder
nodes.is: A card's four rungs. Each rung adds one demand to the one below, coupled to the game's element the same way on every card.

phases.d: Every hull starts at rest.
Every hull starts at level 5 in the game's element.
Team crystals of the game's element on the map.
Fauna of the game's element. Unlocked by plays at I3 or a stat goal.

phases.n: The quest is ready to claim

nodes.repsOf: rungs per card; I4 after a set number of plays at I3

now.note: The standard element ladder is in (2026-11-16). Rung bars are checked from recorded flights; most ladders wait for a person to fly all four.

plan.note: One human plays the four rungs and signs them off as fun; only then is that vessel and element sent to AI training.

nodes.name: Time game
nodes.is: A race. The vessel's mobility against a course and against rivals.

now.note: Every vessel but the Jewel Wasp and the Starling has one. AI drives trained for ten hulls, model only, editor check pending.

plan.note: Trains for Regatta. The arena balances mobility.

nodes.name: Charge game
nodes.is: Pilot against pilot. PvP is petals only: a scored hit takes a petal and silences the victim's abilities for what the hit is worth.

phases.n: A petal leaves them as a crystal

now.note: Every vessel but the Starling has one. None has an AI trained on it and none is signed off.

plan.note: Trains for Broadside. The arena balances pvp: petals taken.

nodes.name: Mass-Space game
nodes.is: A team match for the cell. Fauna born under your nucleus claim score for your team. Making volume and removing rival volume count as one pair.

phases.n: Make your volume or remove theirs
The claim tips to your domain
Fauna are born in your colour: a brood
Hold it for the next brood

nodes.repsOf: broods to win with three teams

now.note: The category exists, and the volume books (made, removed, lost per pilot) are on Brood Rush's scoreboard. Most vessels still have separate Mass and Space cards with their old rules.

plan.note: Each vessel's Mass and Space games become one Mass-Space game: Brood Rush's rule in an environment built for that vessel. Up to 9 vessels, 3 a team. Dolphin first, then Scarab.

holes.q: Only the category has landed. The per-vessel merge has not started: the board still shows Mass and Space as two games each.

nodes.name: Party game
nodes.is: Scurry, Scarab Scramble, Maelstrom. No element, no rules it must keep; each exception is said on the card.

now.note: Maelstrom is always unlocked and runs as a shuffle: placement points across games, first to the target.

plan.note: Trains for nothing downstream, by decision.

nodes.name: Arena
nodes.is: Squad against squad, several vessel classes on one card. Where the fleet is balanced against itself.

phases.d: Three seats. An arena hull is flown once in the whole match.
The vessel carousel; AI fills empty seats.
D-pad left or right moves you to another seat.

now.note: Regatta, Broadside, Brood Rush and Astro League are on the roster. Regatta's course-pool search is the first environment creator and waits on a playtest. Broadside and Brood Rush have not started steps 4 and 5.

plan.note: Three polished arena games, one per element pair, each with an environment creator trained against a fixed pool of elemental AIs. No artifacts in the Arena.

prop.note: An arena match offers the voyage that squad is ready for.

holes.q: Matches per set, and what makes a squad stay for another, are not written.
holes.fill: Best of three against the same opponents, hulls re-drafted between matches, so the set is a loop of its own.

nodes.name: Regatta
nodes.is: The Time arena: every racing hull on one course drawn from a searched pool.

now.note: Eleven hulls seated. Best course pool 1.104x against the 1.10x bar in the model; live, waits on Garrett's playtest and on step 3 for every hull.

plan.note: Balances mobility. What the plateau leaves over is vessel imbalance, tuned on the vessel and sent back through steps 2 to 4.

nodes.name: Broadside
nodes.is: The Charge arena: squads take petals off each other.

phases.n: Set it up with your squad

now.note: Seven hulls seated. Steps 4 and 5 not started.

plan.note: Balances pvp ability: petals taken.

nodes.name: Brood Rush
nodes.is: The Mass and Space arena: teams fight for the nucleus claim and score when fauna are born under it.

phases.n: Cultivators add volume, destroyers remove it
A brood is born in your colour

nodes.repsOf: broods to win with three teams

now.note: Seven hulls seated; three teams and the volume books landed 2026-11-18. Steps 4 and 5 not started.

plan.note: Balances net control of space. Each vessel's place between cultivator and destroyer is measured from play, never set.

nodes.name: Astro League
nodes.is: An arena card outside the three elemental arenas. The Swordfish flies it.

holes.q: The plan names three arena games. Where Astro League sits (a fourth arena, or an arena-sized party game) is not said.
holes.fill: Call it the Arena's party game: it balances nothing and is kept for fellowship, the way party cards are in the Arcade.

nodes.name: A voyage
nodes.is: The culminating experience. A squad of three and one Ark sail the shared HyperSea from port to places and home again. What is aboard when you dock is yours.

phases.d: Your pilots drum up jobs for their factions.
Flown with the Ark, cell after cell.
The location's experience.

phases.n: Push on or turn for home

phases.d: Extraction: only now is the find yours.

now.note: V1 is built as the slice and D1 deepens it on the device: the living galaxy, rival crews by the same rules, work verbs, sagas, standing. Run once in Unity by Garrett. The networked Ark, rival Arks in the world and meeting other squads are not built.

plan.note: V2 to V4: squads meet on arrival, placed by galactic traffic control so the meeting makes sense to both sides' missions. 3 to 6 legs, 20 to 40 minutes.

prop.note: Docking offers the Hangar when the pay covers a vessel, and the next saga chapter when one opened.

holes.q: It is not said whether voyage pay is the same crystals that buy vessels, so the step from 'voyage ends' to 'spend it on a vessel' has no confirmed path.
holes.fill: One soft currency. Voyage pay is crystals, paid at dock, scaled so a clean voyage is worth about three arcade wins.

nodes.name: Port
nodes.is: Choosing the work. News arrives, each seated pilot finds jobs for their faction, and the board shows pay against risk.

phases.n: See the jobs your pilots found

now.note: Jobs for all 16 faction types in nine work verbs; pay follows the course and the standing.

nodes.name: A leg
nodes.is: One lane, flown. The Ark moves, cells stream ahead and recycle behind, and the crossing is where the stakes are.

now.note: Flown Arkway style; wingmates fly escort roles.

plan.note: 2 to 5 minutes a lane. Leaving and arriving are where a squad's instance may change.

nodes.name: A cell
nodes.is: The round of a voyage. The squad takes the cell's nucleus for its domain, the Ark regrows inside it, and the voyage moves to the next cell.

phases.d: Destroyers reduce the opposing volume, cultivators make volume for the team. Both serve the same claim.
Hull plates regrow only inside a nucleus its domain holds.

now.note: Cells stream along a leg and the Ark regrows only in a held nucleus (the escort's rule). The docs do not confirm that taking the cell is what releases the squad to the next one.

plan.note: Garrett, 2026-11-18: once they take over the cell and their Ark regenerates, the larger voyage loop resets and they proceed to the next cell.

holes.q: Cells per leg is not set.
holes.fill: 2 to 4 cells a leg, more on a rough lane, so a leg stays inside 2 to 5 minutes at 45 to 90 seconds a cell.

holes.q: Whether 'take the cell, the Ark regrows, move on' is the built loop or the intended one needs one editor run to confirm.

nodes.name: A location
nodes.is: A cell with an arrangement and a reason to come: a harbour, a vault field, a lair, a wreck, a contested core, a fold. Nothing is scripted; the fundamentals play it out.

phases.d: Pressure sets how rough it is.

now.note: Runs the same with one squad or two; today it is always one.

nodes.name: A meeting
nodes.is: Another squad is there. Traffic control chose the meeting so it makes sense to both missions: a race for vaults, a raid, a truce.

plan.note: V2 and V3. One squad hosts, one joins, in a managed peer-to-peer instance.

nodes.name: The way home
nodes.is: A decision with teeth. A laden Ark draws pirates, and only docking extracts. A fall or an abandoned voyage loses what is aboard.

phases.n: Read the rumour about your own Ark

now.note: Two or more artifacts aboard starts a rumour that pirate crews read.

nodes.name: Activation
nodes.is: The first hours. A spotlight guide to the first game, a Lesson per ship with a ghost that flies the step once, then a Mentor's tips.

phases.n: The spotlight leads to one card

phases.d: The autopilot flies the step once, then hands over the stick.

nodes.repsOf: per player; one Lesson per ship

now.note: Built and merged, never run in the editor. The master unlock is on in shipped builds, so a fresh install gets every lock open and no guidance.

plan.note: The Microgame Training plan. The gate is flipped once the chain is signed off.

holes.q: No player has seen the onboarding. The first loop a stranger meets is an unlocked menu.
The Lesson teaches a ship's Time verb. Nothing yet teaches a combo or a role.
holes.fill: The Mentor's stream is ordered by the ladder of tiers: Pulse and Verb in the Lesson, the kit's first Combo after three races, the Role the first time the player enters a Mass-Space game.

nodes.name: The quest chain
nodes.is: Games unlock in a chain. Reaching a mode's top rung completes its quest; claiming it opens the next. There is no XP.

phases.n: At the end: the Hangar opens

now.note: Scurry, Hex Race, Joust, Maelstrom, then the Vessel Hangar. Stood down by the master unlock.

holes.q: The chain orders 4 cards. About 80 others have no order, so after the Hangar opens nothing says what to play next.
holes.fill: After the Hangar, the chain is per vessel: each hull's flower (see The vessel's flower) is its own short chain of three element games.

nodes.name: The fleet
nodes.is: Winning pays crystals, crystals buy vessels, and a new vessel is a new kit with its own games to learn.

phases.n: Buy a vessel in the Hangar
Learn its kit in its games

nodes.repsOf: wins per vessel (200 a win, 4000 a vessel)

now.note: The economy is live: the winner is paid 200, everyone else nothing; five vessels cost 4000 each. Twenty-three hulls exist; most are not priced or in the shipping list.

prop.note: Crystals get a second sink so the loop does not end with the last vessel.

holes.q: Crystals buy only vessels. When the fleet is owned the reward has no use, and the payout stops driving anything.
holes.fill: Three more sinks: refitting the Ark (hold and plates), recruiting a pilot at port, and colour sets.

holes.q: Which of the 23 hulls ship, at what price and in what order, is not decided beyond the first five.
holes.fill: Price by how many loops a hull opens: a solo hull 4000, a crew vessel 6000 because it opens a second seat for a friend.

nodes.name: The fleet's kits
nodes.is: Every vessel, each with its own loops. Pick one to make it the vessel shown everywhere in the atlas.

nodes.name: The vessel's flower
nodes.is: Proposed. Each vessel has a flower of three petals: Time, Charge, Mass-Space. A petal lights when its game is cleared at I3. It is the player's own pass through the elemental loop.

phases.d: Petal 1. Offers Regatta.
Petal 2. Offers Broadside.
Petal 3. Offers Brood Rush.
The hull is marked voyage-ready in the squad book.

prop.note: Proposal P8. It gives every card an order, makes 'arcade trains for arena' visible to the player, and reuses the petal shape the HUD already teaches.

nodes.name: The squad book
nodes.is: A squad is a deck: three seats, each a vessel, an element, a pilot and an optional artifact. You build several and pick one before a game.

now.note: The squad book and the callsign pilots are built; unverified in the editor. Artifacts apply in voyages only.

nodes.name: Crew and standing
nodes.is: Pilots are people. Recruiting one brings their faction's jobs; succeeding for a faction raises standing, which widens the work and the pay. Pirate work raises notoriety, and a bounty.

phases.n: Seat them: their faction's jobs appear

phases.d: Stranger, Known, Trusted.

phases.n: Promote a captain: join a faction

nodes.repsOf: successes for one faction to reach Trusted

now.note: Device-side stand-in built 2026-11-07: unique people on 18 callsigns, standing, notoriety, grudges. The backend faction roster and the captain UI are not built.

nodes.name: The hoard
nodes.is: Artifacts are found in the HyperSea, carried home at risk, and then carried into the next voyage at risk again.

phases.n: Carry it out again: it can be lost

now.note: Finds, the stake and extraction are built in the slice.

nodes.name: A saga
nodes.is: One story across several voyages. Each chapter is news that becomes a job, found only with the right faction's pilot seated, and the last chapter holds a relic that exists once.

phases.n: Seat the pilot it asks for

nodes.repsOf: chapters per saga; four sagas authored

now.note: Four sagas of three chapters, each ending in a named relic. A saga runs once.

holes.q: A saga does not run again, so four sagas are a fixed amount of story. 'A season could reseed it' is a default, not a decision.
holes.fill: Each Tide reseeds one saga and adds one, so there is always an unfinished thread.

nodes.name: Party and friends
nodes.is: Invite a friend, play as a party, rematch, and come back because they did.

phases.d: AI fills the empty seats.

phases.n: They are on your friends list

now.note: The party lobby, invites, friends and AI backfill exist. Crew vessels (two to four seats on one hull) are local only until networked.

prop.note: A crew vessel's empty seat is the invite: 'fly the kite on my Wrasse'.

holes.q: Nothing a party does together lasts past the sitting, so a friend is a reason to play tonight and not a reason to return.
holes.fill: A party shares one voyage record: the Ark, its hoard and the saga thread belong to the party that sailed it.

nodes.name: Replays
nodes.is: Every match is recorded on the device. Watch your last ten from any camera.

now.note: On Will Bogen's Theater. Reached from Profile and the Arcade.

prop.note: The breath offers 'watch the pass that beat you': a ten-second cut, not the whole match.

holes.q: A replay cannot leave the device, so it drives mastery and nothing else.
holes.fill: Share a ten-second cut as a link that opens the same card at the same rung for whoever taps it.

nodes.name: Episodes
nodes.is: Real money. One token buys one episode. Built as an entitlement; nothing is for sale.

now.note: One episode asset priced at 0. No storefront is wired, and the web checkout is not Steam-compliant.

holes.q: What an episode gives the player is not defined in loop terms: it opens no loop on this map.
holes.fill: An episode is a Tide's content, sold once the Tide has run free for its season: its saga, its arena environments, its colour set.

nodes.name: The living sea
nodes.is: The galaxy moves without you. Every day pressure drifts, blooms ripen, vault fields restock, wrecks are grazed down and rival crews sail. Every change is news.

phases.n: News is born from what happened

nodes.repsOf: tick per day, at most five while away

now.note: On the device, deterministic per day. The same galaxy on the same day on every machine.

plan.note: V3 moves the galaxy to the backend so that locations remember, and the galactic war begins.

nodes.name: The meta turns
nodes.is: The studio's elemental loop, seen from the player's side: arena play exposes imbalance, vessels are retuned, and a new vessel disturbs more than itself.

phases.n: What is left over is vessel imbalance
Ladders and AIs are redone for them
A new vessel enters at step 1

plan.note: Garrett, 2026-11-12: it will disrupt the meta on an optimized schedule before it gets stale. Each loop needs fewer people.

prop.note: Tie each turn to a Tide so that players can see it coming.

holes.q: The schedule is not set, and nothing tells a player that the meta turned or why their vessel flies differently.
holes.fill: One turn per Tide, six weeks. The Tide's news says in authored words which vessels changed and which arena environments are new.

nodes.name: The Tide
nodes.is: Proposed. The clock of the long game, shown on Home as news from the sea: a weekly beat inside a six-week season.

phases.n: Each day: one job that expires
phases.d: From the living sea's tick.

phases.n: Each week: the card of the week
phases.d: One arcade card and one arena environment pool.
Retuned vessels, a reseeded saga, sometimes a new hull.
Its content becomes an episode.

prop.note: Proposal P6. It gives the long game's empty last phase a rhythm built from systems that already tick.

A squad that works in the Arena is the squad you take to sea.
After a voyage: back to a card to learn the hull that let you down.
Spend mission rewards on a new vessel.
What is aboard at the dock joins the hoard.
A job done for a faction raises standing with it.
The winner is paid crystals.
Rung I4 completes the mode's quest.
A new vessel brings its own games to learn.
The squad you saved is the squad you launch.
Each seated pilot finds their faction's jobs.
What happened in the sea arrives as news, and news becomes jobs.
A chapter is a job on the board.
A new or retuned vessel is a kit to learn again.
An invite opens the game.
Each petal offers the arena game it trained for.
The day's job and the week's card are reasons to open the game.
The offered next step after a round.

free.name: Flying for its own sake
free.is: No objective. The only driver is whether the kit is a pleasure by itself.

phases.n: See a shape in the mass

time.name: Racing role
time.is: The kit's Time verb, spent where the course rewards it. One pass is one gate.

phases.n: See the gate and the line to it
Bank what your Time verb needs
Through the gate with speed kept

charge.name: Duelling role
charge.is: The kit's Charge verb, landed on a rival's hull. One pass is one scored hit.

phases.n: Take the petal while they are silenced

ms.name: Cell role
ms.is: Where this vessel sits between cultivator and destroyer. Both serve one claim: a vessel may be poor at one if it is great at the other.

phases.n: Read the claim: who holds the nucleus
Choose: make our volume or remove theirs
Do it with your Mass or Space verb

phases.d: Volume made, volume removed.

party.name: Party role
party.is: Whatever the card's one idea asks of the hull.

cell.name: Escort role
cell.is: The cell role with the Ark in it: take the nucleus for the domain, and keep fauna off the hull while it regrows.

phases.n: Read the cell: claim, fauna, the Ark's plates
The claim and the Ark answer

roleHoles.q: How many passes of the role make a round is counted for races (gates) and not for the other games.
roleHoles.fill: Count scored hits and claim shifts per match from the scoreboard's own events, and aim each game at 6 to 10 passes in its 90 seconds.

roleHoles.q: Where this vessel sits between cultivator and destroyer is to be measured from play. It has not been measured, and the player is never shown it.
roleHoles.fill: Show each pilot their two volume numbers live as one meter, and print the vessel's measured lean on its Hangar card once 100 matches exist.

kit.is: The vessel's four elemental verbs, its omni crystal, its combos and its feel. The kit as designed never changes for a game mode.

holes.q: The combos baked into this kit are not written down anywhere, so nothing checks that a game rewards them or that the ability icons teach them.
holes.fill: Each kit doc names two combos: a feeder into a spender, and one that crosses two elements. The ones shown here are invented from the ability texts for the vessel's owner to correct.

pulse.name: Flight feel
pulse.is: Stick in, hull answers, camera, sound and haptics confirm. Skimming close to mass pays a pulse; ramming it costs a thud.

phases.d: Camera, sound, the skim pulse or the punish thud.

holes.q: What this hull should feel like with nothing to do is not stated per vessel, and only the Dolphin has been signed off as fun.
holes.fill: One sentence per hull in its kit doc: the feeling of its cruise, and the one motion that is a pleasure to repeat.

verbHole.q: This verb's loop is written as what it does, not as steps, and the feeling it should provoke, and at which step, is not written.

hold_release.feel: Tension while it builds, then the snap of letting go.

mode.feel: Changing shape to fit the moment.

phases: The other seat sees the chance

hold.feel: Power under the thumb, and the nerve to let go.

passive.feel: The world pays you for flying well.

omni.feel: A jackpot you had to win a race for.

phases: Pick the card the swarm lacks
card.feel: A plan coming together without your hands on it.

tap.feel: A clean decision, answered at once.

Dolphin.leanWhy: No mass-making ability; its Mass game is excused.

phases: Hold to drift at the speed you came in with
Time.feel: The slide and the kick out of it.

phases: The fan-shaped blast spends the whole bank
Space.feel: The size of the blast is the size of what you banked.

combos.name: The echo shot
combos.is: The Dolphin's full attack: power, target, ammunition, alignment, explosion.
chain: Seek a crystal that can hit that target
Aim onto the crystal so the two are on a collision course
combos.feel: Seeing the line before you fly it, and being right.

combos.name: The hunter's shot
combos.is: The same loop pointed at enemy vessels.
chain: Find a crystal on their line

combos.name: The snap shot
combos.is: Skip the skimming. The shot is smaller, and you fire more often. Which one to use depends on what you are shooting.

Squirrel.leanWhy: Steals mass and destroys none; its Space game is excused.

combos.name: The tube run
combos.is: Speed made from mass, spent on a rival.
chain: Overtake a rival at joust speed
combos.feel: Threading the needle at full speed.

combos.name: The thief's lap
combos.is: Every pass along a rival's trail makes it yours and makes you faster.
chain: Skim a rival trail to steal it
Loop back along what is now your mass

combos.name: The fuse
combos.is: Arm quietly, plant on many, set them all off at once.
chain: Graze a rival to plant a bomb
combos.feel: Nobody knew until it went off.

combos.name: The bait
combos.is: Leave a decoy and let greed do the work.
chain: Collect a crystal: a decoy is left
A rival takes the decoy into danger prisms
combos.feel: A trap someone chose to walk into.

combos.name: The windrow
combos.is: Speed turns the field into a thrown wall.
chain: Hit the field with the blade
Hold a trigger: throw it all to one side
Thrown prisms carry into the next and break both

Urchin.leanWhy: Lays and steals mass and destroys none; its Space game is excused.

combos.name: The rail thief
combos.is: Make a rail, ride everyone's, leave with their mass.
chain: Ride it and any trail: yours grows, theirs is stolen, ammo refills
Slip off clear of the mass
combos.feel: Grinding a line nobody else can.

combos.name: Guns to rockets
combos.is: Gunfire on mass stocks the rocket you spend on a pilot.
combos.feel: Earning the big shot with the small ones.

combos.name: The bunker
combos.is: Stop, build with bullets, roll out.
combos.feel: A wall where there was none.

combos.name: Feed the tank
combos.is: Your own trail is fuel.
chain: Stop: the Seed Wall eats your trail and earns pellets

combos.name: The ghost shot
combos.is: Vanish, aim from nowhere, fire once.
chain: Cloak: a decoy and a seed stay behind
One round through everything on the line
combos.feel: One shot they never saw coming.

combos.name: The crack
combos.is: Plant, wind, release.
chain: Plant the ball and orbit it faster each lap
Winch tight: the ball cracks up to speed
The red ball goes through their mass and their hull

combos.name: Bank and burst
combos.is: Build first, and the next break is bigger.
chain: Mass Mode: the ball steals, shields and banks energy
A bigger blast from what was banked

combos.name: The lit run
combos.is: A straight line that ends in a cut and leaves a wall.
chain: Cut through the field or a rival
combos.feel: A charge with a blade at the end of it.

combos.name: The shift line
combos.is: Four modes, each the answer to the last one's cost.
chain: Space Mode: five guns until they overheat
Creation Mode: five trails while the guns cool
Charge Mode when a rival comes close

combos.name: The ring throw
combos.is: A spare ring is a thrown saw.
chain: An omni crystal adds a spare ring
Throw it: a disk wrecks every prism in its plane

combos.name: The ball game
combos.is: Make a ball, strike it, make it pay.
chain: An omni crystal becomes a ball

Stoat.leanWhy: Its Mass verb touches no mass; its Mass game is excused.

combos.name: The slingshot
combos.is: Lay it, catch it, time it, and the collapse hits everyone near.
chain: Orbit, and let go when the circle turns lime
The pair collapses: a ripple strips rivals

combos.name: The nest strike
combos.is: Leave nests, then paint one target for all of them.
chain: Sling to a block and dock
Detach: a nest is left, growing a missile
Paint a rival: every nest launches
combos.feel: A trap sprung from three sides.

combos.name: Perch and lance
combos.is: Docked, everything recharges faster.
combos.feel: A sniper who is never where they fired from.

combos.name: The school play
combos.is: You fight with what you have gathered.
chain: Light the lure: tame and grow the school
Paint prisms, let go: half the school is thrown at them
Lock a rival: a creature hunts them

Grizzly.leanWhy: Its weapons only destroy; its Mass game is excused.

combos.name: The siege
combos.is: Rush in, dig in, fire, rush out.
chain: Cycle to the claw: the burn spreads

combos.name: The burrow
combos.is: A tunnel is a road, a cannon and a fort.
chain: Form a tunnel and dive: it fires prisms out the far end
A hexagon of your prisms at the exit

combos.name: Paint and tend
combos.is: Lay a field, then fly back over it and make it better.
chain: Mass mode: paint a wide wake
Dust over your prisms grows and shields them; over theirs it destroys

combos.name: The dust trap
combos.is: Fall onto their line and let the dust do it.
chain: Keep them in your dust: petals leave them one at a time
combos.feel: Falling out of the sky onto someone.

combos.name: Perch to perch
combos.is: One seat lays the path, the other plays it.
chain: The Goby darts: a path is laid
The Pistol rides it; mass is pulled into its plane
A vortex ring homes on the Goby's lock
At the perch the Pistol builds a den
combos.feel: Two games that need each other.

combos.name: The one-colour loop
combos.is: The navigator chooses which verb fires by what the kite's tail closes around.
chain: The Grouper flies the hull to the motes
The kite lassos motes of one element
The loop closes: that element's verb fires
combos.feel: Closing the loop just in time.

combos.name: The broadside
combos.is: The helm puts the guns where they can work.
chain: Helm: ring the hull in shield
Gunners: launch and fly the missiles

combos.name: Puzzle to dart
combos.is: The Ratel's puzzle loads the Honeyguide's shots.
chain: The Ratel plays: cards bank stronger uses
Flit, or Peck, with what was banked
Slip along a trail to the next hive
combos.feel: My partner made that shot possible.

Jacks.leanWhy: A herd is not mass; its Mass game is excused.

combos.name: Herd and sting
combos.is: Find them, shape them, send them.
chain: The Call rushes it between the jacks

combos.name: Hand by hand
combos.is: The swarm flies itself; you choose what it becomes. The kit is not settled.
chain: Pick the card the swarm lacks
Time cards bring the next hand sooner

proposals.title: One ladder of words
proposals.what: Use the eight tier terms (Pulse, Verb, Combo, Role, Round, Session, Arc, Era) in every design doc, ticket and review, so a problem is placed before it is argued.

proposals.title: Every verb names its feeling
proposals.what: Each ability's doc gets its loop as steps and one sentence: the feeling, and the step where it lands. The fun card asks about that step.

proposals.title: Every kit names two combos
proposals.what: A feeder into a spender, and one that crosses two elements. Ability icons and the Mentor teach them; a game's course is checked against them.

proposals.title: Show the role
proposals.what: The two volume numbers the scoreboard already books become one live meter, and the vessel's measured lean goes on its Hangar card.

proposals.title: The breath between rounds
proposals.what: After every result, one offered next step: rematch, next rung, or a crossing to the place the round trained for.

proposals.title: The Tide
proposals.what: A daily job, a weekly card and a six-week season, built from the living sea's tick and the studio's rebalance.

proposals.title: More to spend crystals on
proposals.what: Ark refits, recruiting pilots and colour sets, so the payout still drives something after the last vessel.

proposals.title: The vessel's flower
proposals.what: Three petals per hull, lit by clearing its Time, Charge and Mass-Space games at I3. The player's own pass through the elemental loop.

proposals.title: Set the counts
proposals.what: Cells per leg, rounds per run, matches per set, passes per round: each gets a target number and an analytics event that measures it.

proposals.title: One currency
proposals.what: Voyage pay is the same crystals as arcade pay, so 'the voyage ended, buy a vessel' is a real path.

proposals.title: A party owns something
proposals.what: A party shares one voyage record, and a crew vessel's empty seat is an invite.

proposals.title: A replay can travel
proposals.what: A ten-second cut shared as a link that opens the same card at the same rung.
